note: Hand review of every row, beside the mechanical classification the gate is computed on. `reviewed_class` is the class a person reading the root file listing would give it; `reason` says why when the two disagree; `boundary` marks a row that is genuinely arguable. Nothing here feeds the gate - tests/test_artifact_tally.py asserts that - and the audit's purpose is to make the mechanical rule's error rate and its direction visible. Written by reading the cached root listings only, with no network access and no serving figure consulted.
young_arm_review: The young arm is 14 executable and 4 document mechanically. Read by hand it is 13 and 5: one disagreement, and it runs against the hypothesis, so H1's verdict does not depend on it. The four documents by hand are diet103/claude-code-infrastructure-showcase, ChrisWiles/claude-code-showcase, Cloudgeni-ai/infrastructure-agents-guide and Aryia-Behroziuan/References, plus Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts.

donnemartin/system-design-primer.reason: A curated list of interview questions with prose solutions. `generate-epub.sh` and `epub-metadata.yaml` build a book from the markdown; no manifest and no release. The clearest `document` in the population and the highest-starred row in it.

seanooi/iOS-WebP.reason: `iOS-WebP.podspec` is a package manifest, so this is a CocoaPods library rather than prose. DISAGREES with the mechanical class: `*.podspec` is not in MARKERS. The error shrinks `document`.

lorien/awesome-web-scraping.reason: An awesome list. `package.json`, `Makefile`, `lychee.toml` and `tools/` belong to its link checker, not to anything the reader installs to do web scraping. DISAGREES with the mechanical class: a build file for checking links is not a build of the need. The error grows `document`.

cirosantilli/china-dictatorship.reason: Content-only in substance - markdown text and images - but it has a Jekyll `Gemfile`, `package.json`, `index.js`, `setup.py`, a `Makefile` and one release, and it really does publish. The hardest case for the classification and kept as `executable` because the rule as declared reads releases and manifests, not intent.

landy22granatt/Kumpulan-Script-Termux.reason: `README.md` plus `dkfb.bin`. A Termux script collection; the `.bin` name gives nothing to classify and no manifest is present.

donnemartin/interactive-coding-challenge.reason: Exercise solutions in `__init__.py` with `requirements.txt` and `templates/`. Runnable code, but its value is as a study document. Kept `executable` because the solutions execute.

eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain.reason: An Obsidian vault with `pyproject.toml`, `install.sh`, `hooks/` and 13 releases. It ships something installable, which is what the class asks, though most of its bytes are prose.

upptime/upptime.reason: No manifest in the root - `.templaterc.json` and `.upptimerc.yml` are Netlify config - but 39 releases. Classified `executable` on the release channel alone, which is the declared second route.

dariusk/express-activitypub.reason: Both halves came back REFUSED on the first run, and that was this instrument's core budget running out rather than anything about the repository - the row next to it in the same run read fine. The fetcher's first version would have cached that answer permanently; `rootlisting._complete` now refuses to. Re-asked in a later budget window.

Piebald-AI/claude-code-system-prompts.reason: `.gitignore, CHANGELOG.md, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE, README.md, system-prompts, tools`. The highest-starred row in the young arm after `alibaba/open-code-review`, 100 GitHub releases, and not one manifest, entry point or `bin/`. DISAGREES with the mechanical class: a release count is a tag count, and tagging a prompt collection 100 times is not building anything. This is the single row where the release channel misfires, and it is the second-highest-starred row in the arm - which is why the arm's document share is reported both mechanically and by hand.

diet103/claude-code-infrastructure-showc.reason: `.agents, .claude, .codex, .env.example, CLAUDE_INTEGRATION_GUIDE.md, dev, editor-config, setup.ts`. A `setup.ts` is arguably an entry point and `setup` is not one of the declared stems, so the rule called it a document. Kept: what it installs is a configuration layout, which is the thing a person copies, and the repository's own title says showcase.

FlorianBruniaux/claude-code-ultimate-gui.reason: Named a guide, but the root carries `mcp-server/`, `scripts/`, `tools/`, `quiz/`, `exports/`, `machine-readable/`, `llms.txt` and 4 releases, so part of it installs and runs. The hardest `executable` in the arm; recorded as such rather than reclassified towards the hypothesis.

LeeYudok/agents-scaffold.reason: `bin/`, `scripts/`, `presets/`, `tests/` and 2 releases. A scaffold you install.

anderseknert/pre-commit-opa.reason: `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `.pre-commit-hooks.yaml` and 4 releases. A pre-commit hook is installed and run, whatever the root listing's markers say.

Notifuse/selfhost_s3.reason: A budget refusal in the first window, like `dariusk/express-activitypub`. Re-asked.

landy22granatt/Kumpulan-Script-Termux.reason: `README.md` plus `dkfb.bin`. A Termux script collection; the `.bin` name gives nothing to classify and no manifest is present. The release half of the row was also a budget refusal and was re-asked.
